about: Source archive for sketch 42 · Atmospheric Counter-modification. Each entry is cited by id in pm25.json, events.json and the page. 'checked' records how the claim was verified in this sketch: 'read' = the page was read on 2026-11-16 and the value confirmed; 'unreachable' = the page could not be loaded from here; 'secondary' = known only through another source.

sources.title: Ice in the sky: Thailand's fight against air pollution
sources.supports: AFP photo caption: taken 15 January 2025, aircraft spraying icy water over the outskirts of Bangkok.

sources.title: Dry ice and cold water: Thailand's experimental approach to fighting air pollution in Bangkok
sources.supports: Release from about 1,500 m; about 1 tonne per load; twice a day from three bases; critics say 'little to no evidence' it works.

sources.title: Dry ice in the sky: Bangkok's bold new operation for PM2.5 battle
sources.supports: Permission for flights over Bangkok reported on 6 January: 20×20 km area, 3,000–4,000 ft, dry ice at about −70 °C.

sources.title: Royal rainmaking dust control over Bangkok
sources.supports: Permission until April 2025, coordinated with Don Mueang.

sources.title: Bangkok to see royal rainmaking flights amid PM2.5 crisis
sources.supports: 'First time ever' authorised in Bangkok airspace; inner Bangkok below 3,000 ft; no more than 20 minutes; daily flights at 10am and 2pm; water spray and dry ice to 'create atmospheric channels'.

sources.title: Royal rainmaking operation over Bangkok, 24 January 2025
sources.supports: 10:30 operation with four aircraft (CASA ×3, CARAVAN ×1) from Kanchanaburi, Hua Hin and Rayong units; water and dry ice at the inversion layer; night flights requested, not confirmed.

sources.title: Royal rainmaking flight patterns over Bangkok
sources.supports: Inversion described 'like a steamer lid'; spiral and zigzag patterns; flights at 10:00 and 14:00, 1–2 hours; 10 aircraft serving Bangkok.

sources.title: Season plan for royal rainmaking against PM2.5
sources.supports: 13 aircraft (2 CN235, 5 CASA, 6 CARAVAN) at six bases; 'dry ice or water spray' to release dust above the inversion layer.

sources.publisher: Department of Royal Rainmaking and Agricultural Aviation
sources.title: Daily operations report
sources.supports: Since 2 Dec 2024: 865 flights in 53 days, 654,760 litres of water and ice (all regions).

sources.publisher: Department of Royal Rainmaking and Agricultural Aviation
sources.title: Daily operations report
sources.supports: Since 2 Dec 2024: 981 flights in 60 days, 735,500 litres (all regions). Difference with 24 Jan report ≈ 116 flights, all regions, not Bangkok only (calculated here).

sources.title: Royal rainmaking department on its Bangkok operations
sources.supports: 10 aircraft: 5 at Bo Fai (Hua Hin), 3 Kanchanaburi, 2 Rayong; department claims it 'successfully broken the atmospheric inversion layer'; 'stopping burning is the most effective solution'.

sources.title: RTAF sends 2 aircraft with dry ice
sources.supports: Royal Thai Air Force BT-67 ×2, about 2,000 kg of dry ice or agent per flight, 26–30 January; Bangkok flight areas still being coordinated.

sources.title: Cold air mass from China (Thai Meteorological Department)
sources.supports: 'Moderately strong cold air mass from China'; temperatures drop 1–6 °C.

sources.title: Pollution Control Department on improving air
sources.supports: 'Favourable meteorological conditions, stronger winds, and improved ventilation rates'.

sources.title: Governor Chadchart on winds; BMA schools reopen
sources.supports: 'Strong winds had improved air quality slightly'; all 437 BMA schools open.

sources.title: Free public transport 25–31 January 2025
sources.supports: Free MRT, private rail and BMTA buses 25–31 January; 140 million baht compensation.

sources.title: Bangkok pollution forces closure of 352 schools
sources.supports: 352 schools closed in 31 districts on Friday 24 January; work from home urged.
